newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Session is quiet ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Session is quiet ahead of weekend.

text.p: After hours trading was quiet on Friday, with most significant company news relating to halted stocks.
"Nobody is saying much, there's nothing much going on," a dealer said. "It's Friday afternoon."

Avant! Corp, an automation software developer whose stock was halted, waited until after the market closed to announce that it had signed a long-term extension of a pact to supply Lucent Technologies with IC design automation tools.

In addition, Edison Brothers Stores Inc, whose stock was also halted, said its creditors and equity holders had reached a tentative agreement that might ultimately result in the company emerging from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

The after-hours calm marked a contrasted, however, from sharp gains seen on Wall Street during regular trading. After a mixed employment report, the Dow rallied 130 points to 7436, while the Nasdaq jumped 15 points to 1405.
The New York Stock Exchange said that session one volume reached 53,000 on Friday, up from Thursday's 1,300. Session two volume, meanwhile, dropped to 491,300 from 6.45 million the previous day.
